solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps Band Aid record brought back tears when broadcast

definitions.note: Band-Aid is a brand of sticking plaster, so it is an example, flagged by perhaps

indicators.note: brought back says the letters for record are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the letters of tears are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A charity single by Band Aid is replayed on air and moves listeners to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Band Aid looks like the 1984 charity supergroup; here it is the brand of adhesive dressing. 'when broadcast' rearranges TEARS into ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Band-Aid is a trade name for an adhesive dressing, which the British call a sticking plaster.

clue.text: One might get hooked ascending mountain rocks

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means the mountain word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink on the rocks

explanation.surface: A climber on a mountain may get caught on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooked' suggests a climber or an addict; it means caught on a fishing hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish caught by anglers, so it is one creature that might end up on a hook.

clue.text: Bill the setter is captivated by an Alsatian's sharpness

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: is captivated by means the setter is held captive inside the French word

parts.note: Alsace is in France, so an Alsatian's word for an is the French un
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A man called Bill is charmed by his Alsatian dog's sharp wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alsatian' looks like the dog breed; it means from Alsace, a French region, so 'an' becomes UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or shrewdness, so it is a sharpness of mind.

clue.text: Committed a sin in health resort, sweet knocked back outside

indicators.note: outside says the reversed sweet goes around the health resort
knocked back means the word for sweet is read in reverse

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding or dessert
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Someone sinned at a spa by gulping down a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like gulping a pudding down; it reverses the sweet into TRESSED, which 'outside' wraps around the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass, in biblical language as in the Lord's Prayer, is to sin.

clue.text: Poet, sort of, visits religious class

indicators.note: visits means the suffix goes into the school subject like a guest

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, a school subject
the suffix -ish means sort of, as in greenish

explanation.surface: A poet of sorts drops in on a religious class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet, sort of' wants to be the definition; 'sort of' is ISH and 'Poet' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu tradition a rishi is an inspired sage or seer, credited with composing the Vedic hymns.

clue.text: Giant pig bites dog back

indicators.note: back says the whole combination is then read in reverse
bites means the pig holds the dog between its jaws, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a hog is a pig
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A huge pig sinks its teeth into a dog in retaliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is the verb, to follow. 'bites' makes HTAILOG, and 'back' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath is the Philistine giant slain by David, and his name is used for any giant.

clue.text: Posh lass catches game fish — it's arduous

indicators.note: catches means the posh girl holds the game inside her

parts.note: gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl
RU is rugby union
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An upper-class girl lands a hard-fighting game fish, a tiring job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game fish' looks like one phrase but splits into a sport and a separate fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruelling task is exhausting and demanding, which is to say arduous.

clue.text: Music player's turned up in every lughole

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the music player is

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician's playing is turned up so loud it fills every ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like volume; in a down clue it reads ERYL, from across 'every lughole', upwards. Lughole is British slang for ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a small stringed instrument, so it is something that plays music.

clue.text: Refuse to touch silver that's sparkling

indicators.note: to touch means the two pieces are placed side by side, in contact

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is refuse or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone declines to lay a finger on sparkling silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb; it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter is a literary adjective for something glittering, which means sparkling.

clue.text: Fabulous school they monopolise maintains growth

indicators.note: maintains means holds within, so the word for growth sits inside

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it to yourself, so they monopolise means they hog
a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A legendary school whose big players keep growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from a fable or story, not just wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwarts is the school of witchcraft and wizardry in the Harry Potter stories, so a fictional school.

clue.text: River shown on street-map in blue

indicators.note: in an across clue, shown on means placed after, so the river comes after the map

parts.note: an A-Z is a book of street maps of a British city
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river is marked in blue on a street map.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the standard British book of street maps, named for its index.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the colour of a clear sky, a bright shade of blue.

clue.text: Lord's position found — second row, not innermost, amongst others

definitions.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground, so a fielding position there

indicators.note: not innermost says the central letter of the seven-letter word for row is dropped

parts.note: a row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel
e.g., exempli gratia, introduces examples, i.e. some amongst others

explanation.surface: Someone finds a seat at Lord's in the second row among other spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not innermost' takes the middle R from QUARREL, leaving QUAREL. Lord's is a cricket ground in London, and square leg is a cricket fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: Square leg is a fielding position on the leg side level with the batsman, found at any cricket ground including Lord's.

clue.text: US city informally joins race to develop cheese

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters of race are reworked

parts.note: Philly is the informal name for Philadelphia

explanation.surface: An American city casually takes part in a race to produce a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges RACE into CAER.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a crumbly white cheese named after a town in South Wales.

clue.text: Tips found in Sunday tabloid's online agony columns

definitions.note: plural sense: a covered walkway lined by a row of pillars

indicators.note: tips are the ends of things, here the opening letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: Advice turns up in a Sunday paper's online problem pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like advice from an agony aunt; it takes the first letters of four words. 'agony columns' looks like one phrase, but 'columns' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a Greek portico, a colonnade of pillars, so a set of columns.

clue.text: In periphery of Tours, try dear French soap

indicators.note: In means the joined pieces go inside the outer letters
periphery of means the outer letters, the first and last of the city name

parts.note: to try a case is to hear it in court
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: Someone around Tours tries out an expensive French soap.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera set in a farming village.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archers is the world's longest-running radio drama serial, a soap opera on BBC Radio 4.

clue.text: Half of Brummie FC players wearing this spoilt surprise

indicators.note: half of says only the first five of the ten letters of the club name are used

parts.note: Aston Villa is a football club from Birmingham, whose people are Brummies

indicators.note: wearing means the shuffled word is put on around the players like clothing
spoilt means damaged out of shape, so the letters of this are rearranged

parts.note: men are players in a team

explanation.surface: Fans are shocked to see a Birmingham side's players wearing this ruined kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' makes ISHT, and 'wearing' puts the players inside it. A Brummie is someone from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is a feeling of great surprise, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Cooling liquid infused with Eastern energy from an ancient time

indicators.note: infused with means the letter for Eastern is steeped into the mix
liquid means flowing and shapeless, so the letters of cooling are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cooling liquid laced with Eastern energy, from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' rearranges COOLING into OLIGOCN, and 'infused with' puts E inside to give OLIGOCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oligocene is a geological epoch some 34 to 23 million years ago, so a far-off period.

clue.text: Seaman, having fall around sailing boat, is to give up

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: around means the word for fall goes around the boat

parts.note: to fall in battle is to die
a cat is a catamaran or catboat, a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A sailor who has taken a tumble near a yacht decides to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' looks like a tumble; it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce a throne or responsibility, i.e. to give it up.

clue.text: Disconnected scanner during station business

indicators.note: during means the scanner sits within the business abbreviation

parts.note: Co. is a company, a business
a CAT scanner is a medical body scanner

explanation.surface: A scanner cut off while station business goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disconnected' looks like a broken link; it is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In music staccato notes are played short and detached from each other, hence disconnected.

clue.text: Activity of chip-shop crowd that's used to buffet

parts.note: a fish and chip shop coats fish in batter, so battering is what it does
to ram is to cram or crowd things in

explanation.surface: The busy crowd at a chip shop gets pushed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' is the verb, to strike repeatedly, not a spread of food. A chip shop is a British takeaway selling fried fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A battering ram is a heavy beam swung against gates or walls to strike them repeatedly.

clue.text: Perfect golf club used, skirting front of trap

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge, so the golf club surrounds the letter

parts.note: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club

indicators.note: front of takes the opening letter of trap

explanation.surface: A golfer picks the perfect club, steering round a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: A trap is a bunker in golf; here only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is an informal British term for exactly right, so perfect.

clue.text: Indian restaurant might make this soul artist welcome

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is the spirit or soul
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
hi is a greeting or welcome

explanation.surface: A curry house might host a soul singer and greet him warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soul artist' looks like a singer, but the two words are clued separately: an Egyptian spirit and an Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A karahi is a curry cooked and served in the wok-like pan of that name, a dish found in Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Long time to grasp German pronoun? On the contrary

indicators.note: to grasp means holding something inside, so one piece goes within another
On the contrary reverses the roles: the pronoun holds the time instead of the other way round

parts.note: ich is German for I

explanation.surface: A query about how long it takes to learn a German pronoun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a length of time; it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to crave it, the same yearning as to long for it.

clue.text: Garden of Eden Charlie wanted over time, with grass in abundance

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop, and cereals are grasses

indicators.note: Charlie is wanted over time, i.e. preferred in its place, so the letter for time is swapped out

parts.note: the Garden of Eden is a perfect place, a utopia
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie longs for paradise, time and plenty of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted over' replaces the T in UTOPIA with C, giving UCOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia, the horn of plenty, stands for an overflowing supply, hence abundance.

clue.text: VIP raised stink after arrest

indicators.note: after says the reversed stink comes after the arrest

parts.note: to nab is to arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters for stink go upwards, reversed

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stink

explanation.surface: A celebrity kicked up a fuss after being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised stink' looks like making a fuss; it reverses BO into OB.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a wealthy or important person, from the term for Mughal governors in India.

clue.text: Inferior type of driver from Italy

parts.note: L is a learner driver, from the L-plate
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A second-rate kind of motorist from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: An L-plate marks a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo-fi, low fidelity, describes sound recordings of poorer quality, so inferior.

clue.text: Visiting Balliol regularly with old captain in poor spirits

parts.note: to be visiting a place is to be at it

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the college name, starting from the second

parts.note: Captain Matthew Webb was the first person to swim the English Channel, in 1875

explanation.surface: Someone at an Oxford college with an old sea captain feels low.
explanation.walkthrough: Balliol is an Oxford college; its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters give ALO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at a low ebb, like a tide that has gone out, is to be depressed or in low spirits.

clue.text: Maybe no ball skill's brought about by English number ten

definitions.note: a no ball is one kind of run conceded in cricket without the bat, flagged by maybe

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the word for skill is reversed

parts.note: skill is art, the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's call caused by an English bowler wearing the number ten shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, such as no balls and wides. 'brought about' reverses ART into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A no ball, an illegal delivery, gives the batting side a run counted among the extras.

clue.text: Eating away, European crew gets through wine

indicators.note: gets through means the crew passes into the middle of the wine

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
IV is four in Roman numerals, a rowing crew of four

explanation.surface: A European crew gets through a lot of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A four is a rowing boat with four oarsmen, so IV can stand for a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erosive wears material down gradually, eating it away as water erodes rock.

clue.text: Dog's half-finished relishes seen in bowl mostly

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: dog is

indicators.note: seen in means the fragment of relishes is placed inside the shortened bowl
mostly says the bowl word loses its final letter

parts.note: a basin is a bowl

indicators.note: half-finished says only the first half of the six-letter word for relishes is used

parts.note: to relish something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: A dog enjoys half its food, which can still be seen in its bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the bowl to BASI, 'half-finished' keeps the first three letters of the verb, and 'seen in' puts them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a small barkless hunting dog from central Africa.
